prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1472; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's representing attorney after a side impact at an intersection; the attorney confirmed the claimant was the driver of the vehicle struck on the passenger side and that a neck strain is being claimed.
Entry 2: Verified that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the loss; nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates coverage.
Entry 3: Police report and two statements from the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact, though no independent witnesses to the collision itself have come forward.
Entry 4: Scene and vehicle photos were reviewed; they confirm several details of the described impact, and the damage pattern on the vehicle is consistent with a side impact of this type.
Entry 5: Claimant's medical records show a neck strain that is plausible for a crash of this kind; no prior injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history or prior claims search.
Entry 6: Treatment followed a usual course, with therapy visits tapering as the claimant's symptoms improved; no unusual billing patterns have been noted to date.
Entry 7: Claimant provided a few additional details in a follow-up interview, but the core account of the collision has remained the same across all statements; no earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and the file is being kept open pending final treatment records.
